title: Suzuki Jimny JB74 / JB64
verdict: Suzuki styled it like a 1970s LJ, kept the ladder frame and two solid axles, and then watched the whole world queue for it. It's slow, it's tiny and it's illegal to import into America until 2043, which only makes people want one more.

paragraphs: Production of the fourth-generation Jimny started at Suzuki's Kosai plant on 29 May 2018, the first time Jimnys had been built there, and the truck went on sale in Japan on 5 July, the first all-new Jimny in twenty years. Its styling looks back to the [[suzuki/lj-series|LJ]] and [[suzuki/samurai|SJ/Samurai]] generations, with flat panels, round lamps and drip rails. Underneath, Suzuki kept the ladder frame, the front-engine rear-drive layout, the part-time 4WD with a low-range transfer gear, and three-link solid axles at both ends. Then demand outran supply in almost every market it entered, and it hasn't fully caught up since.

story.heading: KEI JB64 VS SIERRA JB74
paragraphs: As with the [[suzuki/jimny-jb23|JB23]] generation, there are two widths. The JB64 is the kei car, sold only in Japan: 3,395 mm long and 1,475 mm wide, with no fender flares, tucked-in bumpers and a turbocharged 658 cc R06A three-cylinder, in XG, XL and XC trims. The JB74 is the one the world knows. Japan calls it the Jimny Sierra (JL and JC trims), and everyone else simply calls it the Jimny. It's 1,645 mm wide with bolt-on flares and has the 1.5-liter K15B.

Both share the 2,250 mm wheelbase, a reworked ladder frame with extra cross members that Wikipedia's development notes credit with about 1.5 times the torsional rigidity, a choice of five-speed manual or four-speed automatic, and standard brake-LSD traction control. That system brakes a spinning wheel so the one opposite can keep pulling, which is useful but no substitute for a locker. Suzuki Australia quotes 210 mm of ground clearance, with approach, breakover and departure angles of 36°, 27° and 47°.

story.heading: THE K15B
paragraphs: The K15B replaced the [[suzuki/jimny-jb23|JB43]]'s M13A. It's a 1,462 cc all-aluminum DOHC 16-valve four with variable valve timing, a 74 x 85 mm bore and stroke, a 10:1 compression ratio and a timing chain. In Suzuki Australia's spec it makes 75 kW (102 PS) at 6,000 rpm and 130 Nm (96 lb-ft) at 4,000 rpm. That's a real gain over the old 1.3, but it's still only 1,095 kg of truck being pulled up hills by a naturally aspirated four.

Unsealed 4X4's staff, many of them Suzuki owners, are blunt about it. The engine is 'begging for a few more killer-wasps, or even better, a turbo.' The four-speed automatic is 'way too old to be put into a vehicle in this decade,' and next to it the manual 'feels like it has an extra 30kw available.' Gearing is the other complaint: the transfer case is 'geared way too high for anywhere near sizeable tyres,' so a set of lower gears tends to arrive alongside the first set of bigger tires.

story.heading: THE QUEUE
paragraphs: Suzuki UK's entire 2019 allocation of 1,200 cars was sold by December 2018, with waits of up to a year, and some dealers stopped taking deposits. Suzuki blamed a bottleneck at the Japanese factory. In Australia the queue was still up to twelve months in mid-2021, and in Mexico the first 1,000 reserved units sold out in three days. At home, Japanese Jimny sales went from about 11,000–16,000 a year in the old truck's last decade to 30,281 in 2019 and roughly 40,000 a year from 2021. Maruti Suzuki began building Jimnys in India in January 2021 to help supply export markets.

Europe shows the other side of the coin. At 154–178 g/km of CO2, the Jimny dragged Suzuki's fleet average well above the EU target, so the passenger car was withdrawn from the UK in 2020 and returned as a two-seat light commercial vehicle. That too was withdrawn from European sale in 2025.

story.heading: FIVE DOORS, AND THE AMERICAN QUESTION
paragraphs: The five-door Jimny (JC74) was revealed in India in January 2023 and launched there on 7 June 2023. Its wheelbase is 340 mm longer at 2,590 mm, and it's built only at Maruti Suzuki's plant in Gurugram for export to almost 100 countries. Australia got it in December 2023 as the Jimny XL. Japan got it on 30 January 2025 as the Jimny Nomade and took about 50,000 orders in four days, against roughly 1,200 cars a month allocated for Japan. Suzuki suspended orders, apologized, raised output to about 3,300 a month and reopened the books on 30 January 2026.

For Americans, none of this is available. Suzuki left the US car market in 2012, and the JB74 was never certified here. In September 2022, CBP seized a 2022 Jimny that a US citizen had bought in Mexico and driven across the border, because DOT ruled it ineligible: it was 'less than 25 years old from the date of manufacture.' The earliest JB74s turn 25 in mid-2043. Until then, the legal way into a small Suzuki in the US is a 25-year-old [[suzuki/jimny-jb23|JB23 or JB43]].

callout.label: SIDEBAR · CO2 AND THE TWO-SEAT JIMNY
callout.title: How Europe turned the Jimny into a van
paragraphs: In July 2020 Suzuki stopped taking new UK orders for the passenger Jimny. Even its cleanest version, the manual, emitted 154 g/km of CO2, 59 g/km above the fleet average Suzuki had to hit the following year, and the WLTP figure Autocar reported at launch was 178 g/km. Every Jimny sold made Suzuki's fines bigger.

Suzuki's answer, from September 2020, was the Jimny Commercial: the same truck re-homologated as an N1 light commercial vehicle, with no rear seats, a partition behind the front seats and up to 863 liters of load space. Vans face a looser target of 147 g/km rather than 95 g/km. It cost £16,796 plus VAT and kept the ladder frame, solid axles and ALLGRIP PRO low range. Wikipedia records it being withdrawn from European sale in 2025.

engineering_intro: The fourth generation keeps the classic Jimny layout: a separate ladder frame, now with extra cross members, and rigid axles front and rear on coil springs, each located by three links. Drive is rear-wheel by default, with a part-time 4WD system Suzuki calls ALLGRIP PRO adding the front axle and a low range. There's no center differential, and traction control brakes spinning wheels instead of locking diffs.

engineering.v: Ladder frame with added cross members
engineering.note: About 1.5 times the torsional rigidity of the old frame, with redesigned body mounts, per Wikipedia's development notes.
Same layout front and rear. Unsealed found the stock XL 'ran out of travel quickly' off-road.
2WD-High, 4WD-High and 4WD-Low, no center diff. Manual low range is 2.002:1 per BigJimny's gearing table.
Standard on all versions; brakes the slipping wheel of a diagonal pair. Open diffs; no factory lockers.
Chain-driven DOHC with VVT. Japan's kei JB64 uses the 658 cc R06A turbo three instead.
Suzuki Australia figures for the 3-door. The 5-door XL keeps the approach and departure angles but drops breakover to 24°.

generations_table.note: No fender flares, 1,475 mm wide. Sold only in Japan, in XG, XL and XC trims.
Global 3-door, 1,645 mm wide. Built in Japan, and in India from January 2021.
Two-seat N1 van with up to 863 L of load space, created to cut Suzuki's fleet CO2.
2,590 mm wheelbase, built only in India. India from June 2023, Australia December 2023, Japan January 2025.

buying_checks.head: Check the recall record
buying_checks.body: EU Safety Gate lists three Jimny recalls: fuel pumps whose resin impellers could swell and stall the engine (cars built 9 May to 22 November 2018, then a second campaign for 12 November 2018 to 7 September 2019), and door wiring harnesses that could break and stop the side and curtain airbags deploying (cars built to 2 December 2020). Ask a dealer to run the VIN.

buying_checks.head: Get underneath with a flashlight
buying_checks.body: BigJimny's wiki says every Jimny generation has 'particularly poor rust prevention' from the factory, and the usual spots are the chassis welds and the body and spring mounts. The JB74 is still young, but a truck from a salted-road region should show evidence of underbody protection.

buying_checks.head: Drive it at 45–50 mph
buying_checks.body: Steering shake in that band was the third generation's signature fault, from kingpin bearings in a poorly sealed knuckle. BigJimny expects the same on the JB74 because the design is so similar, so test-drive at that speed and rock each raised front wheel.

buying_checks.head: Inspect any lift kit properly
buying_checks.body: A good Jimny lift includes caster correction, a crossmember drop, extended brake lines and often a panhard bracket. Pedders notes the factory headlight-leveling bracket can't simply be extended without risk of breaking. Missing pieces mean someone took shortcuts.

buying_checks.head: Do the payload math
buying_checks.body: Unsealed puts the 3-door's factory payload at about 340 kg (750 lb), which a bull bar, winch, roof rack and two adults can use up. In Australia, check for a GVM upgrade plate or engineer's certificate if the truck is heavily accessorized.

buying_checks.head: Big tires without gearing?
buying_checks.body: Anything larger than 215/75R15 really needs lower gearing. Without it, BigJimny owners warn you'll quickly burn the clutch or overheat the automatic's fluid. Ask what ratio changes came with the tires.

buying_checks.head: Manual or automatic
buying_checks.body: Unsealed 4X4 couldn't see 'a viable reason to spend the three extra grand' on the four-speed auto in an XL. The manual is the enthusiast pick, and the autos are slower.

buying_checks.head: In the US? Ask how it got here
buying_checks.body: A 2018-on Jimny can't be legally imported into the US until it's 25 years old. CBP's 2022 Puerto Rico seizure ended with an order to bring the truck into compliance, export it or destroy it. Don't buy one with 'paperwork in progress.'

repairs.title: Diagnose steering wobble (kingpins first)
repairs.time: ≈ Half a day per side for kingpins
repairs.symptoms: A shaking steering wheel around 45–50 mph, play when a raised front wheel is rocked top to bottom with the brakes held, or oil and grease weeping from the swivel balls.
repairs.fix: Follow BigJimny's death-wobble order. Check tire balance first, then rock each front wheel with an assistant holding the brakes: play that remains points to the kingpin bearings, play that disappears points to the wheel bearings. Check tie-rod ends, radius-arm bushes and the hub face behind the brake disc for rust. If the kingpins are worn, rebuild them with Koyo bearings, a new halfshaft seal and waterproof grease.
repairs.tools: Jack and stands · torque wrench · tie-rod end puller · bearing drift.

parts.name: Kingpin Bearings (Koyo) with Swivel Seal Kit, listed for gen 3; confirm gen 4 fitment with the seller

repairs.title: Fit a 40–50 mm lift properly
repairs.cost: Roughly A$1,300–3,000 for a kit, per Unsealed's suspension guide
repairs.symptoms: Not a fault. The stock suspension rides choppily, sags under accessories and limits tire size.
repairs.fix: Choose springs rated for your real load: OME offers three front-spring options for stock, bull-bar and bull-bar-plus-winch trucks. Fit caster-correction bushes or adjustable arms, a crossmember drop for driveshaft angle, extended brake lines for droop and a panhard-rod bracket to correct the rear roll center. Sort the headlight leveling, then get a wheel alignment.
repairs.tools: Spring compressor (if needed) · trolley jack and stands · torque wrench · alignment afterward.

parts.name: Old Man Emu suspension, Suzuki Jimny 2019–present
Suspension lift kit, Jimny JB74 2018+, Nitro Gas Medium

repairs.title: Upgrade the GVM for touring (Australia)
repairs.symptoms: A bull bar, winch, roof rack, fridge and two adults put the truck over its factory gross vehicle mass of 1,435–1,450 kg.
repairs.fix: Fit a federally approved GVM kit with matched springs and shocks. Ironman's kit raises GVM from 1,435 kg to 1,785 kg (axle limits 800 kg front, 1,100 kg rear) and lifts the truck 45 mm; TJM's XGS GVM+ goes to 1,800 kg. Fitted before registration, the truck gets a new compliance plate. Fitted afterward, a state-approved engineer must inspect it and issue a modification plate.
repairs.tools: As for a lift kit · approved installer for certification.

parts.name: Ironman 4x4 (Jimny GVM upgrade kits through approved installers)
TJM XGS suspension and GVM+, Suzuki Jimny

repairs.title: Add a selectable locker
repairs.time: ≈ A day per axle at a shop
repairs.symptoms: Brake-LSD traction control hesitates or runs out of grip on steep, cross-axled climbs. Unsealed found itself waiting for it to kick in, which cost momentum.
repairs.fix: Unsealed's view is that 'with a pair of lockers it'll go pretty much anywhere.' A selectable air locker behaves like an open diff until you switch it on. Setting up the diff, running air lines, fitting a compressor and wiring switches all need skill, so many owners leave it to a shop.
repairs.tools: Diff setup tools (bearing puller, dial indicator) · compressor and air lines · or a 4x4 shop.

repairs.title: Do the first full filter service
repairs.cost: The price of filters and oil
repairs.symptoms: Unknown service history, a dusty air filter after gravel roads, or a musty cabin.
repairs.fix: Change the engine oil and filter, the air filter and the cabin filter using genuine Gen 4 parts, and check the fluid grades and capacities in your owner's handbook. Inspect the air filter at every oil change if you drive on dirt roads.
repairs.tools: Oil filter wrench · drain pan · basic hand tools.

repairs.title: Replace a worn rear wheel bearing
repairs.symptoms: A hum or rumble from the rear that changes with speed, or play at the rear wheel when you rock it.
repairs.fix: Pull the axle shaft, press off the old bearing and retainer, press on the new ABS-type bearing and retainer and fit a new axle oil seal. BigJimny's rear wheel bearing guide covers the gen 3 procedure; check your gen 4 manual for differences.
repairs.tools: Slide hammer or puller · hydraulic press · new retainer ring.

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: Stock is 195/80R15. The BigJimny consensus is that 215/75R15 is the biggest that suits the stock rims, though it's only slightly taller. Some Australian owners squeeze 235/75R15s on, but those exceed the stock rims' recommended limits. With a 2-inch lift, 235/75R15s fit with a little trimming of the front bumper. Go bigger and you'll want lower gearing.

faq.q: Can I import a new Jimny into the US?
faq.a: No. It isn't certified for US safety or emissions rules, and NHTSA's exemption only covers vehicles 25 years old from their date of manufacture, which puts the earliest JB74s (built from 29 May 2018) at mid-2043. In 2022 CBP seized a 2022 Jimny bought in Mexico and taken to Puerto Rico, and ordered it brought into compliance, exported or destroyed.

faq.q: What's the difference between the JB64 and JB74?
faq.a: The JB64 is Japan's kei car, with a 658 cc R06A turbo three, no fender flares and a width of 1,475 mm. The JB74 is the 1.5-liter K15B truck with flares and a width of 1,645 mm, sold as the Jimny Sierra in Japan and as the Jimny everywhere else. They share the 2,250 mm wheelbase and the drivetrain layout.

Unsealed 4X4 thinks the long-wheelbase versions of Suzuki 4x4s have always been 'far superior,' with more stability, better climbing and more room. The XL's 2,590 mm wheelbase drops breakover from 27° to 24°, but rear cargo space with the seats up goes from 85 to 211 liters.

Manual, if you can. The automatic is an old four-speed, and Unsealed says the five-speed manual feels like it has an extra 30 kW by comparison. Suzuki Australia rates the manual at 6.4 L/100 km and the auto at 6.9.

faq.q: How much can it tow and carry?
faq.a: Suzuki Australia rates it at 1,300 kg (2,866 lb) braked and 350 kg (772 lb) unbraked, with a 1,450 kg GVM for the 3-door. Unsealed puts real payload at about 340 kg, which a bull bar and winch eat quickly. Towing anything bigger than a small trailer is 'not the droid you're looking for.'

faq.q: Why is it so hard to get one?
faq.a: Demand has run ahead of supply since launch. The UK's 2019 allocation sold out by December 2018, Australia had up to a 12-month queue in 2021, and Japan's 5-door Nomade drew about 50,000 orders in four days in 2025, forcing Suzuki to stop taking orders for a year.

faq.q: Why was it pulled from Europe?
faq.a: CO2. Even the cleanest manual emitted 154 g/km, far above Suzuki's EU fleet target, so the passenger car was withdrawn from the UK in 2020 and replaced by a two-seat commercial version facing a looser 147 g/km target. Wikipedia records that version leaving European sale in 2025.
No. Both diffs are open, and 'brake LSD' traction control brakes a spinning wheel to send torque to the others. ARB lists Air Lockers for the 2019-on Jimny if you want the real thing.

Euro NCAP gave the 2018 3-door Jimny three stars, with 73% for adult occupant protection. Standard equipment varies by market and year. Australian cars now have six airbags, AEB and lane-departure warning, and the 2026 Australian 3-door update added adaptive cruise and front and rear parking sensors.
Japanese tuner DAMD sells 'little G.' body kits for the Jimny Sierra that restyle it as a miniature [[g-class/w463|G-Class]].

mods.why: 40–50 mm of lift with load-rated springs improves ride, clearance and tire room. Look for kits that include caster correction, brake lines and a panhard bracket.
Legally doubles usable payload for touring in Australia. Ironman's kit takes payload from about 340 kg to 690 kg.
Brake-based traction control is good, but selectable lockers are what turn a Jimny into a rock-hopper.
A bull bar for winch mounting and animal strikes, plus underbody protection. Factor the weight into your payload.
Japan's tuning scene loves restyling the Jimny. DAMD's 'little G.' kits for the Jimny Sierra are the best known.
Genuine Gen 4 filters and bearings, plus kingpin parts, shipped from the UK.

baseline_service.intro: No US dealer will ever service one, so the owner's handbook is your bible. Suzuki UK's handbook locator has the official fluid grades and capacities. We haven't been able to source the JB74's capacities independently, so treat the specs below as types to confirm. On a used truck with gaps in its history, BigJimny's rule for every Jimny applies: change every fluid and filter now.

items.interval: Per handbook; shorten for dusty or towing use
Inspect at every oil change if you drive on dirt
items.note: BigJimny's gen 3 practice of changing it at around 25,000–30,000 km, or sooner in dust, is a sensible baseline.
Purely for the occupants, but worth doing on a dusty truck.
The K15B is chain-driven, so there's no timing belt to budget for.
Suzuki's gen 3 manuals required silicate-free coolant from 2005, according to BigJimny. Don't top up with a generic green.

items.interval: Shorten if you've fitted bigger tires
items.note: Larger tires without regearing make the clutch and automatic work harder, so fresh fluid is cheap insurance.
Gen 3 owners change it every 3–5 years despite Suzuki saying 'never.'

items.spec: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] (gen 3 used API GL-5 80W-90 hypoid)
items.interval: Change on an unknown truck and after deep water
items.note: Replace the drain gasket each time.

items.interval: At every service once the truck sees off-road use
items.note: BigJimny expects the gen 3's kingpin wear to carry over because the design is so similar.
Rear brakes are leading/trailing drums, so check the shoes and wheel cylinders while you're there.

items.spec: Fuel pump (2018–2019 builds) · door harness/airbags (to Dec 2020)
items.note: Have the dealer run the VIN; recall work is free.

items.spec: Coat the chassis and wax the cavities
items.interval: As soon as possible, then check yearly
items.note: BigJimny: do it while the truck is still clean. Don't wait for rust to start.
